title: TypeScript SDK: first-class streaming interoperability guide and adapter surface
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem statement:
Teams are asked to support both AsyncIterator-based consumption (for Node and older browser polyfills) and Web Streams (ReadableStream) in the TypeScript SDK. Over the past year we've accumulated multiple ad-hoc helpers and example snippets across docs and PRs which are hard to discover and inconsistent in behavior around cancellation, backpressure, and retries. This ticket centralizes a single, well-documented adapter surface and canonical examples for both Node and browser runtimes.

Goals:
- Define small set of stable helpers: toAsyncIterable(), toWebReadable(), framedStream(), and streamWithRetry().
- Ensure adapters preserve cancellation semantics (AbortSignal), propagate upstream backpressure where possible, and expose a predictable end/error contract.
- Provide clear examples for: streaming text generation, binary chunked embedding streams, and bidi transform flows.
- Include guidance for Node (stream.Readable) interop and for browsers (TransformStream/ReadableStream).
- Add integration tests and a perf harness that exercises typical payloads (short chat turns and long generations) and validates no memory leak on resumed/resilient streams.

Non-goals:
- Building a full-featured resumable generation protocol (out of scope for this ticket; will be tracked separately).
- Implementing server-side protocol changes — adapters assume current streaming framing format.

Proposed API (surface):
- export function toAsyncIterable<T>(rs: ReadableStream<T> | AsyncIterable<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<T>
- export function toWebReadable<T>(it: AsyncIterable<T> | ReadableStream<T>, options?: { highWaterMark?: number, signal?: AbortSignal }): ReadableStream<T>
- export function framedStream(source: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, decode: (chunk: Uint8Array) => string): AsyncIterable<string>
- export async function* streamWithRetry<T>(factory: () => AsyncIterable<T>, opts?: { attempts?: number, shouldRetry?: (err: any) => boolean, resumeTokenExtractor?: (item: T) => string | undefined }): AsyncIterable<T>

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Backpressure: when converting AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream we will use ReadableStream pull() to request from iterator only when controller.desiredSize > 0. For ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable we will buffer up to a configurable highWaterMark and await controller.wait if the consumer falls behind.
- Cancellation: adapters accept an AbortSignal. When signaled, they should close the underlying stream/iterator if possible and surface an AbortError to the consumer. This mirrors fetch/ReadableStream behavior.
- Retry semantics: we will provide a simple best-effort retry wrapper that can re-invoke the network factory and, if the protocol provides a resume token, continue from the last seen token. We will not attempt speculative merging of partially-decoded chunks.
- Binary vs text: framedStream() decouples low-level chunk boundary handling from decoding so users can reuse for binary embeddings or byte-delimited responses.
- Node compatibility: provide small helpers that convert to/from Node's stream.Readable (node:stream) using an adapter that respects .pause()/.resume() and uses async iterator APIs when available.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public typings and exported helpers exist in packages/sdk-js/streaming with unit tests covering cancellation, backpressure, and error propagation.
- End-to-end integration tests against the live dev staging API that validate text streaming and binary embedding streaming.
- Examples added to docs/examples/ for: Node text consumer (async iterator), browser consumer (ReadableStream + TransformStream), and a duplex demo (async iterator -> TransformStream -> ReadableStream).
- Benchmark run (CI job) demonstrating no increase in median token latency by >10% and memory stable under long runs (30 minutes of continuous streaming at 50 concurrent clients).
- API reviewed and approved by SDK lead and runtime team (review comments addressed).

Risks:
- Subtle differences between browsers' ReadableStream implementations (Chrome vs Safari) may require runtime shims — tests must cover modern Safari.
- Retry/resume can be hazardous for non-idempotent streams; explicit guidance and clear opt-in required.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Exports and docs for toAsyncIterable/toWebReadable/framedStream/streamWithRetry published. 2) Unit tests: cancellation, backpressure, error semantics. 3) Integration tests run on staging and pass. 4) Example recipes for Node/browser/duplex are merged to docs. 5) PR approved by SDK lead and runtime engineers.
notes: Design decisions recorded in the design doc favor simple ergonomic defaults: adapters should be low-ceremony (single import), explicit about needing an AbortSignal for cancel, and opt-in for retry behavior. We prefer to expose small primitives over monolithic helpers so teams can compose: framedStream() + streamWithRetry() is the recommended pattern for resilient text streaming.
